ℒ.name: Lagrangian density
ℒ.meaning: The action per unit volume and time. Nature takes the path where its integral, the action, is stationary - every equation of motion follows.

μν.name: Spacetime index pair
μν.meaning: Two spacetime indices, each running over t, x, y, z. A repeated upper and lower index is summed (Einstein convention).

ij.name: Index pair
ij.meaning: Two indices labelling rows and columns of a matrix (e.g. particle generations).

∂.name: Partial derivative operator
∂.meaning: ∂_μ = ∂/∂x^μ: the rate of change along one spacetime direction.

χ.name: Chi
χ.meaning: A field or susceptibility; here usually a dark-sector field that interacts only through gravity.

mχ.name: Dark scalar mass
mχ.meaning: The mass of the dark-sector particle χ.

μc.name: Chemical potential
μc.meaning: The free energy added by one more particle of a species; species flow from high to low μ until it is equal everywhere.

ρI.name: Information erasure density
ρI.meaning: Bits erased per unit volume per unit time. Each costs at least kT ln 2 of free energy.

y.name: Yukawa coupling
y.meaning: How strongly a matter field couples to the scalar field; its value fixes that particle's mass m = yv/√2.
